To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transverse mass of strange particles produced at the SPS in central Pb-Pb collisions can be described by a blast-wave model and that the transverse flow velocity increases with the centrality of the collision.

the blast-wave model provides an adequate description of the data, that the transverse mass distribution of $\Omega$ is harder than that of $\Lambda$, and that the transverse flow of strange baryons increases with the centrality of the event.
the transverse mass distribution of the strange particles is compatible with a blast-wave model and the temperature parameter is independent of centrality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the transversal momentum distributions of strange and non-strange particles produced in Pb–Pb collisions at 40 and 158 $A GeV/c$.
the study of the production of strange hadrons in central Pb-Pb collisions and the comparison to the production of non-strange particles.
the study of the transversal mass distribution of the strange particles in Pb-Pb collision at 158 AGeV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transverse mass distribution of the strange particles is well described in the framework of a thermal blast-wave model with a collective transverse velocity of about 0.6$c$ and a temperature of about 160 MeV.
the transverse mass distribution of the strange particles produced in the most central Pb-Pb collisions, at the SPS energy, is compatible with a thermal source at a temperature of 160-165 MeV.
the blast-wave model provides a reasonable description of the transverse-mass spectra, but that there is no evidence for a significant change of the transverse expansion in more central events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the blast-wave model provides a reasonable description of the data, with a temperature of the system of $165 \pm 10 \, \mathrm{MeV}$ and an average transverse expansion velocity of $0.6 \pm 0.1$ (for the most central events).
the transverse mass of strange hadrons in central Pb-Pb collisions is consistent with the transverse mass measured in p-p collisions at 158 GeV/$c$.
the transverse mass distribution of all particles can be well described with the blast-wave model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the blast wave model provides a good description of the transverse momentum spectra of strange particles, including the $\Xi$ and the $\Omega$, in Pb-Pb central collisions.
, for all particles and for the full event sample, the transverse mass distribution is well described by the blast-wave model.
the transverse mass of the strange particles is a function of the collision centrality.
